title: Co-Scientist: repurposed drugs against liver fibrosis
summary: In Gary Peltz's Stanford lab, two of the three existing drugs proposed by Co-Scientist blocked fibrosis and promoted regeneration in human liver cells, while Peltz's own two choices showed no benefit. The anticancer drug vorinostat blocked 91% of a damage response that can lead to scarring. Cell experiments only; published in Advanced Science.

evidence.tested: The anti-fibrotic efficacy and toxicity of 25 drugs were assessed serially in human liver organoids grown in microwells; Co-Scientist's candidates were tested in cells alongside the authors' own picks.
evidence.ai_role: The AI co-scientist multi-agent system proposed three candidate drugs with reasoning, and helped direct their experimental characterization.
